title: Safeguards for Elderly and Vulnerable Users as More Government Services Move to Singpass Digital Platform
what_it_is: Safeguards for Elderly and Vulnerable Users as More Government Services Move to Singpass Digital Platform

sections.label: Singpass access without mobile phones
sections.summary: Asked how GovTech will ensure residents without mobile phones can access Government e-services via Singpass after the OneKey token ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister with the discontinuation of the OneKey token from 1 April 2021, how will GovTech ensure that (a) all residents who do not own a mobile phone will be able to access Government e-services using Singpass, given that a local mobile phone is required for the Singpass two-factor authentication (2FA) process; and (b) notwithstanding the introduction of Multi-User SMS 2FA, whether alternative 2FA methods can be provided to enable residents with no mobile phones to login with Singpass independently, without the assistance of a third party.

sections.label: OneKey token phase-out date
sections.summary: The token will be phased out, with its last day of use on 31 March 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The token will be phased out and the last day of use will be 31 March 2021.

sections.label: Subsidised smartphone and mobile plan
sections.summary: The subsidised smartphone starts from as low as $20, and the mobile plan from as low as $5 a month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The subsidised smartphone starts from as low as $20, the mobile plan from as low as $5 a month.

sections.label: In-person support for digital services
sections.summary: In-person support will be provided at 55 SG Digital community hubs, PA's Tech Connect initiative and Integrated Public Service Centres, ensuring access to all services.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: For those who need it, we will also provide in-person support at the 55 SG Digital community hubs at our community clubs and libraries islandwide and at PA's Tech Connect initiative and Integrated Public Service Centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Whilst the Government is working towards the digital delivery of all Government services, we will also ensure that everyone always has access to all these services.

sections.label: Alternative 2FA methods and SSO counters
sections.summary: Asked whether GovTech will introduce 2FA methods not requiring a mobile phone or counter visit, and extend counters to all Social Service Offices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand that there are other methods of logging in but none of these fully replace the OneKey token which allows users to log in independently without the mobile phone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, will GovTech consider introducing other 2FA methods that do not require users to have a mobile phone or be physically present at counters?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can such counters also be extended to all Social Service Offices (SSOs) because many residents who visit the SSOs are not tech-savvy but they need to log into the Singpass to retrieve supporting documents like CPF statements and HDB statements?

sections.label: No timeline to phase out counters
sections.summary: The speaker believes there is no timeline to phase out physical counters because some contact, hand-holding, training and engagement will always be needed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: If you ask me, I would believe there is no timeline to phase out physical counters because there will always be a need for some contact, some hand-holding, some training, some engagement.

sections.label: Singpass Mobile data sharing consent
sections.summary: The private sector wants consent-based access to government-verified data fields, so banks prefer customers use Singpass Mobile and authorise data sharing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: You realise many times now, you do not need to keep filling up forms repeatedly because the private sector wants to have access with consent to those fields of data which the Government verifies and that is why the banks today would prefer that you use Singpass Mobile and that you authorise them so that they can get the data that they need in a way which they feel is more accurate.
